document.title: build: warnings, sanitizer option, QuickJS and fetch limits
document.summary: Turns on `-Wall -Wextra` with an opt-in `-Werror`, adds a host `VITADECK_SANITIZE` option run in CI, gives every `vd_thread` an explicit stack, bounds the QuickJS stack and heap, and caps `fetch` response bodies at 4 MiB.
document.why: QuickJS's default stack guard assumes more stack than the 256 KiB Vita thread has, and nothing bounds JS memory or `fetch` bodies ([#53](source:s1)).

sources.title: Compiler warnings, sanitizer builds, and JS memory/stack limits
sources.gist: Enable -Wall -Wextra, add VITADECK_SANITIZE for host CTest, set QuickJS memory and stack limits sized for the Vita thread, cap fetch bodies, make the JS thread stack explicit.

sources.label: PR #76
sources.gist: Implements #53 in three commits, stacked on #75.

lookFor: The ticket also lists "no Debug config for Vita" as part of the problem ([#53](source:s1)); the Vita build still sets only `-O3` and this PR adds no Debug variant there.

groups.title: -Wall -Wextra and the fallout
groups.why: The ticket asks for `-Wall -Wextra` with the fallout fixed ([#53](source:s1)).
groups.summary: `CMakeLists.txt` adds the warning flags globally while moving vendored and third-party headers to `-isystem` and building `quickjs` with `-w`, and the few warnings left in `src/` are fixed at their sites.
lookFor: OpenSSL and host raylib include dirs moved from `-I` to `-isystem` alongside `vendor/`; the Vita SDK dirs stay `-I` so the toolchain's own system-dir order is untouched.

groups.title: VITADECK_SANITIZE and the sanitized CI run
groups.why: The ticket asks for a `VITADECK_SANITIZE` option used by the host CTest job ([#53](source:s1)).
groups.summary: The CMake option adds `-fsanitize=` to every host target, `smoke-docker.sh ctest` builds and runs all harnesses with it, and CI calls that mode as a second step after the golden smoke run.
lookFor: `quickjs` builds with `-fno-sanitize=undefined`, so UBSan never reports inside the interpreter; ASan still instruments it.
`-fno-sanitize-recover=all` makes the first UBSan report abort the test, so a new UB in `src/` fails CI instead of only printing.

`tests/lsan.supp` suppresses any leak with `libLLVM` or `glfwCreateWindow` on its stack; only `smoke_harness` gets it, and no `src/` code runs beneath `glfwCreateWindow`, so a leak allocated by VitaDeck code still fails the run.

groups.title: Explicit thread stack and QuickJS limits
groups.why: Every Vita thread gets 256 KiB while QuickJS's default guard assumes 1 MiB, and `JS_SetMaxStackSize` / `JS_SetMemoryLimit` were never called ([#53](source:s1)).
groups.summary: `VD_THREAD_STACK_SIZE` in `thread.h` sets every `vd_thread`'s stack on both platforms, and `js_thread_func` derives the QuickJS stack limit from it minus 64 KiB and caps the JS heap at 64 MiB.
lookFor: Subtle: the host stack applies to fetch workers and upload handler threads too; on Linux they drop from glibc's 8 MiB default to 1 MiB, on macOS they grow from 512 KiB.
The 64 MiB heap limit also applies on host, so a Deck App that allocates past it now shows `out of memory` on the Deck App Failure Screen during desktop development, matching the Vita.

groups.title: fetch body cap
groups.summary: `fetch_write_cb` stops curl once the body would pass `FETCH_MAX_BODY_BYTES`, and `fetch_worker` turns that into a rejection with a fixed message that `CONTEXT.md` documents for authors.
lookFor: A 200 response with a 5 MiB body now rejects with `fetch response body exceeds the 4 MiB limit` instead of resolving; the `body_too_large` check runs before `res != CURLE_OK`, so curl's own write-error text never reaches JS.

groups.title: js_limits harness
groups.why: Proves that hitting each limit reaches the Deck App Failure Screen state instead of crashing, on the host and on the Vita stack size.
groups.summary: `tests/js_limits_harness.c` writes stand-in `js/runtime.js` files and runs them on the real JS thread, and CMake builds it twice, once forcing `VD_THREAD_STACK_SIZE` to the Vita value, on a source list shared with `smoke_harness`.
lookFor: The fetch cases use `file://` URLs, so they depend on the host libcurl having the file protocol, which Ubuntu and macOS builds do.

commits.subject: ci(smoke): suppress Mesa leak in GLX window init under LSan
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
GitHub's runner leaks 128 bytes inside Mesa during glfwCreateWindow's GLX
init. Suppress by that frame: no VitaDeck code runs beneath it, so leaks
in src/ stay visible.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(core): bound QuickJS stack and memory, cap fetch bodies
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Every vd_thread now gets an explicit stack (256 KiB on Vita, 1 MiB on
host) and QuickJS stops 64 KiB short of it, so deep recursion reaches
the Deck App Failure Screen instead of overflowing the thread. The JS
heap is capped at 64 MiB and fetch rejects bodies over 4 MiB.

js_limits_harness drives the real JS thread with recursive, memory-hungry
and oversized-fetch runtime.js stand-ins, also on the Vita stack size.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: build: add VITADECK_SANITIZE and a sanitized CTest CI step
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Host-only -fsanitize= list for vitadeck and every CTest harness.
QuickJS opts out of UBSan (upstream signed-shift UB) but keeps ASan.
The smoke harness suppresses llvmpipe's libLLVM leaks only.
smoke-docker.sh gains a ctest mode; CI runs it with address,undefined.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: build: enable -Wall -Wextra and a VITADECK_WERROR option
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Vendored and third-party headers are -isystem and QuickJS sources build
with -w, so only our code is diagnosed. CI host job turns on -Werror.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
